assertions.description: The API this restriction applies to.
permissions.query is how a page reads the grant before registering a fetch — the service worker cannot prompt, so this is the only way to branch correctly.
The local-network permission name must be recognised, and querying it must return one of the three states without prompting. A browser that throws on the name has not shipped Local Network Access.
query() reports rather than asks, which is what makes it safe to call on load. Querying twice in a row must return the same state with no user interaction in between.
PermissionStatus is an EventTarget, so a page can react when the grant changes while it is open rather than re-querying on a timer.
The same Local Network Access machinery on the ordinary fetch path. Background Fetch is being brought under it, so the fetch side is the reference point.

backgroundFetch.fetch() is gated on transient user activation, so a scripted call rejects. This is why the attempt demo asks the reader to click rather than starting one itself, and it must not be mistaken for a Local Network Access refusal.
assertions.test: (async()=>{try{const reg=await navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistration('/v154/local-network-access-restrictions-for-background-fetch/');if(!reg||!reg.backgroundFetch)return false;await reg.backgroundFetch.fetch('conf-lna-'+Math.floor(performance.now()),['/public/media/jpeg-xl/image.avif'],{title:'conformance probe',downloadTotal:17317});return false;}catch(e){return e instanceof TypeError;}})()
